paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, baker: the psalmist is in trouble, and he doesn't run from God's Word, he runs INTO it. He's oppressed, he's lowly, he's despised, and he still says, "Trouble and distress have found me, but Your commandments are my delight." (Psalm 119:143) Hard days didn't make him close the book. They made him open it wider.

Why? Because he trusts who God is. He says, "Righteous are You, O LORD, and upright are Your judgments." (Psalm 119:137) He calls God's words "Wonderful" (Psalm 119:129), and he says "The unfolding of Your words gives light; it informs the simple." (Psalm 119:130) You don't need to be the smartest person in the room, friend. You just need to open the Word, and the lights come on.

Look at what he keeps asking for, too: "Give me understanding, that I may live." (Psalm 119:144) He doesn't want a shortcut around trouble, he wants to understand God's Word and to live by it. So when your week gets heavy, I'd say do what he did and bring it all to the LORD and keep leaning on His Word. This psalm isn't done singing yet, so stay tuned.
